verdicts.threatModel: The two advisories (GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2 high, GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2 moderate) are CPU-exhaustion DoS in smol-toml 1.7.0 parse() on malformed or adversarial TOML. An attacker must supply TOML text that reaches smol-toml's parse(); the only attacker capability that could do so here is write access to the repository's own manifests.
verdicts.reachability: smol-toml 1.7.0 enters only as a devDependency of @rightkit/release 0.2.124 (package.json:40 devDependencies; pnpm-lock.yaml:519-521; scanner path '.>@rightkit/release>smol-toml', dev:true). Its sole importer, @rightkit/release/ownership.mjs:4, calls parseToml only on Cargo.toml files of the scanned checkout (ownership.mjs:231,242) during maintainer-run release/ownership tooling. No product code imports it: the Tauri web frontend (apps/lightcraft-desktop/web) references neither smol-toml nor @rightkit/release, and the Rust product does not use npm packages. No network or end-user input reaches the parser.
verdicts.impact: None across a trust boundary. The parsed input is first-party Cargo.toml in the checkout; anyone able to modify it can already execute arbitrary code during the same build via build.rs or Cargo dependencies, so a parser hang grants no new capability. Worst case is a hung local release-tooling process, self-inflicted by whoever wrote the manifest; shipped binaries are unaffected. Scanner severity 'critical' also overstates the advisories (1 high, 1 moderate, 0 critical per scanner metadata).
verdicts.rationale: Vulnerable version is genuinely installed (dependency hygiene: bump @rightkit/release or smol-toml to >=1.9.0), but there is no attacker-controlled source, no trust boundary crossed, and no runtime/product reachability, so the candidate is not a security vulnerability.
verdicts.devilsAdvocate: Could a malicious contributor PR add a crafted Cargo.toml to hang CI? Anyone submitting a PR can already add an infinite loop in build.rs or a test, which CI executes anyway; CI job timeouts bound both. A third-party crate's Cargo.toml is not scanned (only checkout manifests selected from the repo), so supply-chain input does not reach parse().
